title: GST 114 ( UNN ) : CHAPTER SEVEN ( DIRECT AND REPORTED SPEECH )
subject: GST 114

questions.question: Direct speech is defined as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Direct speech involves quoting the exact words spoken by a person.

questions.question: Quotation marks perform which function in direct speech?
questions.explanation: Quotation marks are used to enclose the exact words of a speaker.

questions.question: The first word inside quotation marks must undergo which change?
questions.explanation: The first word of a direct quote must begin with a capital letter.

questions.question: Which punctuation mark follows the reporting clause before a quote?
questions.explanation: A comma typically separates the reporting clause from the quoted speech.

questions.question: The reporting clause identifies which element of direct speech?
questions.explanation: The reporting clause identifies who is speaking.

questions.question: The reporting clause typically contains which elements?
questions.explanation: A reporting clause usually consists of a subject and a reporting verb.

questions.question: Which position can a reporting clause occupy in a sentence?
questions.explanation: The reporting clause can be placed at the beginning, middle, or end of a sentence.

questions.question: When the reporting clause is in the middle, the verb inside the quote takes which form?
questions.explanation: The verb inside the quote remains lowercase when the reporting clause interrupts it.

questions.question: Which verb is commonly used in the reporting clause?
questions.explanation: Verbs like say, tell, and ask are commonly used in reporting clauses.

questions.question: The reporting clause separates the quote from which element?
questions.explanation: The reporting clause separates the quoted words from the identification of the speaker.

questions.question: Quotation marks undergo which change in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: Quotation marks are removed when converting direct speech to indirect speech.

questions.question: Pronouns in indirect speech typically undergo which change?
questions.explanation: Pronouns change in indirect speech to reflect the perspective of the reporter.

questions.question: Time and place indicators in indirect speech typically undergo which change?
questions.explanation: Time and place indicators are altered to fit the context of the reporting.

questions.question: The word "that" replaces which element in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The word "that" is often used to introduce indirect speech, replacing quotation marks.

questions.question: The tense in indirect speech typically undergoes which change?
questions.explanation: The tense typically shifts back one step in indirect speech.

questions.question: Indirect speech is also known as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Indirect speech is also known as reported speech.

questions.question: Indirect speech presents a message in which manner?
questions.explanation: Indirect speech conveys the meaning without quoting the exact words.

questions.question: The present simple tense changes to which tense in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The present simple tense changes to the past simple tense in indirect speech.

questions.question: The present continuous tense changes to which tense in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The present continuous tense changes to the past continuous tense.

questions.question: The present perfect tense changes to which tense in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The present perfect tense changes to the past perfect tense.

questions.question: The modal "will" changes to which word in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The modal "will" changes to "would" in indirect speech.

questions.question: The modal "can" changes to which word in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The modal "can" changes to "could" in indirect speech.

questions.question: The modal "may" changes to which word in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The modal "may" changes to "might" in indirect speech.

questions.question: The modal "must" changes to which word in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The modal "must" changes to "had to" in indirect speech.

questions.question: The word "this" changes to which word in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The demonstrative "this" changes to "that" in indirect speech.

questions.question: The word "here" changes to which word in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The place adverb "here" changes to "there" in indirect speech.

questions.question: The word "now" changes to which word in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The time adverb "now" changes to "then" in indirect speech.

questions.question: The word "today" changes to which phrase in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The time expression "today" changes to "that day" in indirect speech.

questions.question: The word "tomorrow" changes to which phrase in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The time expression "tomorrow" changes to "the next day" in indirect speech.

questions.question: The word "yesterday" changes to which phrase in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The time expression "yesterday" changes to "the previous day".

questions.question: The word "ago" changes to which word in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The time expression "ago" changes to "before" in indirect speech.

questions.question: The phrase "last night" changes to which phrase in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The time expression "last night" changes to "the previous night".

questions.question: The phrase "next week" changes to which phrase in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The time expression "next week" changes to "the following week".

questions.question: The pronoun "I" typically changes to which pronoun in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The pronoun "I" changes based on the speaker's gender and perspective.

questions.question: The pronoun "we" typically changes to which pronoun in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The pronoun "we" typically changes to "they" in indirect speech.

questions.question: The possessive adjective "my" typically changes to which word in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The possessive adjective "my" changes to "his" or "her" depending on the speaker.

questions.question: The possessive adjective "our" typically changes to which word in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The possessive adjective "our" typically changes to "their".

questions.question: The pronoun "you" typically changes to which pronoun in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The pronoun "you" changes to "he" or "she" depending on who is being addressed.

questions.question: Which sentence is an example of direct speech?
questions.explanation: Direct speech uses quotation marks to report exact words.

questions.question: Which sentence is an example of indirect speech?
questions.explanation: Indirect speech does not use quotation marks to report the message.

questions.question: The verb "come" changes to which verb in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The verb "come" changes to "go" in indirect speech.

questions.question: The verb "bring" changes to which verb in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The verb "bring" changes to "take" in indirect speech.

questions.question: The word "thus" changes to which word in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The adverb "thus" changes to "so" in indirect speech.

questions.question: The word "hence" changes to which word in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The adverb "hence" changes to "thence" in indirect speech.

questions.question: The word "hither" changes to which word in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: The adverb "hither" changes to "thither" in indirect speech.

questions.question: Imperative sentences in indirect speech are typically reported using which verb?
questions.explanation: Imperatives are usually reported using verbs like ordered, told, or requested.

questions.question: Interrogative sentences in indirect speech are typically reported using which verb?
questions.explanation: Interrogatives are typically reported using the verb asked.

questions.question: Exclamatory sentences in indirect speech are typically reported using which verb?
questions.explanation: Exclamations are typically reported using the verb exclaimed.

questions.question: The reporting clause is also known as which of the following?
questions.explanation: The reporting clause forms the main clause in a sentence of reported speech.

questions.question: The punctuation mark that follows the reporting clause before a quote is which of the following?
questions.explanation: A comma is used to separate the reporting clause from the direct quote.
